followup_reviews.Research finding: Official notices and later attributed confirmation establish a reconstruction-related restriction at Tazhen–Daut Ata; retain inclusion. The current phase is limited to persons, passenger cars and buses. The initial light-freight restriction is recorded in source history, while later heavy freight activity and technical commissioning are not treated as passenger reopening. The official retrospective statement supports 1 February 2025 start; the 29 December report supplies same-cohort last confirmation. The 331-day calendar difference remains a censored minimum with no endpoint or complete flag. The undated traveller body and the guide’s date attribution do not advance the bound. Administration and service operation remains supported by explicit reconstruction and safety statements. No narrower subcategory or inferred political motive is added. The official extension and December statement were freshly read; initial and November notices, the undated NewTimes body and secondary travel guide were reread from exact receipts. Government statements repeated in news or guide pages are not independent corroboration. The Kazinform article is shared with the Kaplanbek parent under separate source aliases. The current phase stays unlocated; no geometry is inferred from a national renovation programme or from freight handling at one side of the pair.
